weather_report: Subiaco sits in the small hours under a heavy quilt of cloud, the streets hushed, the air smelling faintly of wet iron as light rain sidles in around two. Clarity is softened to a watercolor—streetlamps haloed, edges blurred—so don a light rain jacket, closed shoes, and a gentle layer for the cool, damp air. Toward dawn the drizzle should ease to ragged, broken cloud, letting shy ribbons of sunlight slip through; sunshine will be brief and sifted at first, with UV near nothing now and only slowly waking after sunrise, then building if the cloud thins. It looks quietly pleasant in a muted way, a night made for finishing a note to yourself, laying out tomorrow’s kit, or steeping something warm while the gutters tick. When the rain loosens its grip, a short, unhurried walk on the damp verge or a simple errand by foot will feel right; later in the morning, if the sky opens, carry sunglasses and a dab of sunscreen, then let the day find you rather than the other way round.
